The Claim's word is "a small allowlist (`driver:publish-fold`, `publish:pr`, `publish:hold`, `publish:merge`, `driver:ack-decision`)", and `skills/ultralearn/scripts/fleet_events.py` already carries the sibling convention for this — `test_event_kinds_matches_the_engine_vocabulary` in `tests/test_fleet_events.py:180` pins `EVENT_KINDS` by exact-set equality. The new render-level tests only establish the five ARE exempt (`test_render_timeline_keeps_an_allowlisted_kind_whole`) and that two named kinds are NOT (`publish:comment`, `engine:log`), so a sixth kind silently added to the frozenset leaves every test green while widening the exemption the Claim calls small. The exam's own `WHOLE_KINDS` tuple already spells the five out, so the pin is one assertion. This is advisory only: M3 as written speaks of the five kinds' behaviour, not of the set's extent, and every leg the Proof names is otherwise carried — no criterion is left unverified.

tests/test_harvest_fleet_runs_confine_denials.py:368 — `test_an_unreadable_envelope_is_a_diagnostic_and_never_a_traceback` takes `capsys`, calls `capsys.readouterr()` and throws the result away, so the "loud" half of the global constraint it names ("a source that is absent or unreadable is one line on stderr and never a traceback") is never asserted; only the "never a traceback" half is. Its second assertion, `bundle["confineDenials"] in (None, [])`, is also satisfied by both branches of the `has_source` decision, so it pins nothing about which one an unparseable envelope takes. This leaves no Machine clause unverified (M4 legs (d) and (e) are pinned exactly by their own tests, and the advisory constraint carries no `Check:`), so it is advisory. Fix: capture the output and assert the diagnostic names the envelope path, e.g. `err = capsys.readouterr().err` then `assert "envelope.json" in err`, and assert the exact expected value (`== []`, since `workers/impl_1/envelope.json` exists and therefore a source is present) rather than a two-way `in`.; `test_an_unreadable_envelope_is_a_diagnostic_and_never_a_traceback` in tests/test_harvest_fleet_runs_confine_denials.py names a diagnostic it never asserts: it takes `capsys`, calls `capsys.readouterr()` after the build and discards the result, so deleting the `_warn(f"unreadable {path}: {exc}")` in `_read_json` leaves the test green. Its value assertion is also loose — `bundle["confineDenials"] in (None, [])` — where the outcome is deterministic: `workers/impl_1/envelope.json` exists, so `has_source` is true and the answer is `[]`, and accepting `None` would hide a regression that made a present-but-unreadable source read as "no source at all". Tighten to `err = capsys.readouterr().err; assert "unreadable" in err` and `assert bundle["confineDenials"] == []`. Nothing in the Machine slot rests on this, so it does not block.; The `_envelope_denials` docstring in skills/ultralearn/scripts/harvest_fleet_runs.py claims the derived line is "Shaped exactly as `fleet/run-worker.mjs`'s `recordEnvelopeDenials` shapes the lines it appends to `confine-denials.jsonl`, so a run that has both sources reads uniformly." It is not exact: `recordEnvelopeDenials` (fleet/run-worker.mjs:511) emits a `ts` and caps `reason`/`toolInput` at 200 characters via its `cap` helper, while the derived line has no `ts` and no cap. The absence of the cap is correct here — the global constraint forbids cutting a kept denial line to a length — so only the docstring needs to change; say the line carries the same field NAMES as `recordEnvelopeDenials`, without its `ts` and without its 200-character cap, and why the cap is deliberately absent.; INTERFACES Produces reads "`confineDenials` — the `bundle.json` key, a list of denial lines each carrying `source`, or `null`", but M3 requires the `confine-denials.jsonl` lines be carried "in file order, each as parsed" verbatim, and a pre-#476 file line has no `source` at all — `_make_run_dir`'s row in tests/test_harvest_evidence.py is `{"tool": "Bash", "reason": "outside clone"}`, which `test_a_local_run_dir_bundles_exactly_as_the_base_harvester_did` pins by equality. So the diff can lawfully emit a line without `source`, and it must. The M clauses and the pinned BASE shape govern; the Produces wording is what is over-strong. No edit inside this tree resolves it — recording it so the contract text can be narrowed to "each derived line carrying `source`" when the plan is next touched.; plan-defect: plan-defect: every envelope denial is emitted TWICE on a local run directory that has both `workers/*/envelope.json` and `confine-denials.jsonl`, which is the ordinary shape of a sandbox-logs tarball whenever any worker was denied. `_confine_denials` (skills/ultralearn/scripts/harvest_fleet_runs.py) returns `envelopes + transcripts + file_lines` with no reconciliation, and `fleet/run-worker.mjs:511 recordEnvelopeDenials` already appends one `{"source": "envelope", label, role, tool, reason, toolInput}` line per `permission_denials` entry into that same `confine-denials.jsonl` — the implementer's own docstring on `_envelope_denials` says so ("Shaped exactly as `fleet/run-worker.mjs`'s `recordEnvelopeDenials` shapes the lines it appends to `confine-denials.jsonl`"), and the task Context says the file's lines carry `source: "hook"` or, since #476, `source: "envelope"`. Both legs still pass and no criterion is left unverified, so this is advisory; restore the two dropped asserts alongside the names check.; `_gh_api_object` (skills/ultralearn/scripts/harvest_fleet_runs.py:176) repeats the body of `_gh_api_listing` (:150) and `_gh_api` (:121) verbatim — the same `subprocess.run(["gh", "api", path], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=GH_TIMEOUT)`, the same non-zero-is-an-absence return, the same `json.loads` + `swallow` on a JSONDecodeError — with only the post-parse type check differing. All three functions are inside this task's FILES, so a small `_gh_api_json(api_path)` returning the parsed body (or None) with the three callers keeping only their type checks would remove the third copy without changing any pinned behaviour.
